_comment: ADR-037 register fragment - approval-routes-resolve-a-manager-and-declare-silence. Patches ApprovalRoute and DecisionStage by key union. A step can name a RULE instead of a person, resolved when the step becomes live rather than when the route is instantiated. A route says whether it is required, which is what lets a consuming app ask whether a subject is cleared. A step declares what its silence means once its due date has passed, defaulting to hold so no stored route changes meaning. And a step can ask the actor's substitute part-way through its window, before the deadline rather than after it. See openspec/changes/approval-routes-resolve-a-manager-and-declare-silence/specs/approval-routes/spec.md, REQ-AR-012 through REQ-AR-017.

ApprovalRoute.description: Patched by approval-routes-resolve-a-manager-and-declare-silence: a route says whether it is required, and its steps can name a rule instead of a person, declare what their silence means and ask a substitute before the deadline.

required.title: Required
required.description: Whether this route has to conclude before its subject counts as cleared. Defaults to true, because a route somebody bothered to start is a route somebody is waiting on, and the safe default for a clearance question is the one that blocks (REQ-AR-014).

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The ordered steps, with the rule, silence and substitute additions. Every addition defaults to today's behaviour, so no stored route changes meaning.

actorRule.title: Actor rule
actorRule.description: A rule that resolves to a person when the step becomes live, instead of a person named now. A step carries `actor` or `actorRule` and never both: a step carrying both has two answers to the same question and whichever the engine happens to read first wins, which is a bug nobody can reproduce. Resolved at ACTIVATION rather than at instantiation, so a manager who changes next week reaches the steps that have not been asked yet and leaves the ones already signed alone (REQ-AR-012).

actorRuleSubject.title: Actor rule subject
actorRuleSubject.description: The person the rule is read against, for the rules that need one. `manager-of-subject-owner` reads the subject's own owner instead and needs none.

onSilence.title: On silence
onSilence.description: What this step's silence means once its due date has passed. `hold` is the default and is what every stored route means today: nothing happens and the stage stays active. `approve` is a signature nobody gave, so only an administrator may set it and a route carrying it says so on its own surface (REQ-AR-015).

askSubstituteAfter.title: Ask substitute after
askSubstituteAfter.description: How far into the step's window to ask the actor's substitute as well, as a fraction between 0 and 1. Asking BEFORE the deadline rather than after it is the whole point: a substitute asked after the term has run is a substitute asked too late to help. Unset means no substitute is asked (REQ-AR-016).

DecisionStage.description: Patched by approval-routes-resolve-a-manager-and-declare-silence: a stage records which rule produced its actor and when, what its silence means, whether a substitute was asked or looked for, and whether a lapse has already been applied to it.

actorResolvedBy.title: Actor resolved by
actorResolvedBy.description: Which rule produced this stage's actor, when a rule did. Kept so the stage can answer why this person was asked, which a resolved name on its own cannot (REQ-AR-012).

onSilence.title: On silence
onSilence.description: Copied from the step at instantiation, so editing a route never changes what the silence of a stage already in flight means.

substituteAskedAt.title: Substitute asked at
substituteAskedAt.description: When the substitute was also asked.

substituteActor.title: Substitute actor
substituteActor.description: Who the substitute is. Both they and the original actor may act, and whichever acts first closes the stage.

substituteSearchedAt.title: Substitute searched at
substituteSearchedAt.description: When a substitute was looked for and none was found. A NOTE on the stage rather than a refusal: no substitute is a normal state of affairs and must not stop the original actor from signing (REQ-AR-016).

lapsedAt.title: Lapsed at
lapsedAt.description: When a lapse policy was applied to this stage. Written once, and the sweep skips a stage that already carries it, which is what makes running the sweep twice harmless (REQ-AR-017).
